Implicit weights from a two-period TWFE regression with covariates

Source: R/two_period_covs.R
two_period_reg_weights.Rd

With two periods, a TWFE regression with time-varying covariates is the regression of the change in the outcome on the treatment indicator and the change in the covariates. This function writes its coefficient on the treatment as a reweighting estimator (comparing weighted averages of the change in outcomes for the treated and untreated groups) and reports how well the implicit weights balance covariates (Caetano and Callaway, 2026).

Usage

two_period_reg_weights(
  yname,
  tname,
  idname,
  gname,
  xformula = ~1,
  time_invariant_x_formula = NULL,
  extra_balance_vars_formula = NULL,
  extra_balance_d_vars_formula = NULL,
  balance_d_vars_post = TRUE,
  data,
  weightsname = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

yname

Name of the outcome variable.

tname

Name of the time period variable. The data must have exactly two periods.

idname

Name of the unit identifier.

gname

Name of the group variable: 0 for untreated units and a single positive value (typically the second period) for treated units.

xformula

One-sided formula for the time-varying covariates in the TWFE regression (which enter through their change between the two periods), e.g. ~ x1 + x2. Default ~1 (no covariates).

time_invariant_x_formula

One-sided formula for time-invariant covariates to include with time-varying coefficients (so they do not drop out of the regression), e.g. ~ region. Default NULL.

extra_balance_vars_formula

One-sided formula for additional covariates to report balance for, without including them in the regression. Time-varying covariates enter through their value in the first period. Default NULL.

extra_balance_d_vars_formula

One-sided formula for additional time-varying covariates to report balance for through their second-period level or their change (see balance_d_vars_post). Default NULL.

balance_d_vars_post

For covariates in extra_balance_d_vars_formula: if TRUE (the default), report balance in their second-period level; if FALSE, in their change between the two periods.

data

A balanced panel data.frame in long format.

weightsname

Name of the column holding sampling weights, which must be constant over time within each unit. Default NULL (unweighted).

...

Not used; allows the same arguments as did::att_gt().

Value

An object of class two_period_covs_obj: a list with

est

the TWFE coefficient on the treatment indicator.

weights

the implicit regression weights, one per unit.

dy

the change in the outcome for each unit.

D

the treatment indicator for each unit.

cov_balance_df

a data.frame with one row per variable (the change in the outcome first, then the covariates). Columns: covariate; unweighted and weighted means for the treated and untreated groups and their differences (unweighted_treat, unweighted_untreat, unweighted_diff, weighted_treat, weighted_untreat, weighted_diff); the pooled standard deviation sd (pooled_sd()); and unweighted and weighted versions of the log ratio of standard deviations (log_ratio_sd()) and the fraction of treated units with extreme values (frac_treated_extreme()).

ess

the effective sample size of the untreated group (effective_sample_size()).

Details

The implicit regression weights balance the means of the covariates that enter the regression (here, the changes in the time-varying covariates and any time-invariant covariates in time_invariant_x_formula) between the treated and untreated groups by construction. They do not, in general, balance the levels of the time-varying covariates or other covariates; the balance table and ggtwfeweights() show by how much. When parallel trends holds conditional on covariates that the regression does not balance, the TWFE estimate can be biased even if all treatment effects are the same.

References

Caetano, Carolina and Brantly Callaway. "Difference-in-Differences when Parallel Trends Holds Conditional on Covariates." Working paper (2026). doi:10.48550/arXiv.2406.15288

See also

two_period_aipw_weights() for AIPW, regression adjustment and inverse probability weighting; implicit_twfe_weights() for more than two periods.

Examples

data(castle, package = "causaldata")
castle <- as.data.frame(castle)
# two periods: 2000 (before any state adopted) and 2010
castle2 <- subset(castle, year %in% c(2000, 2010))
castle2$G <- BMisc::get_group(castle2, "sid", tname = "year", treatname = "post")

tw <- two_period_reg_weights(
  yname = "l_homicide", tname = "year", idname = "sid", gname = "G",
  xformula = ~ l_police + unemployrt, data = castle2
)
